rows.note: This is the all-purpose adjective for saying that someone is candid and straightforward.

example.english: I'll be frank with you: this report isn't good enough.
example.traditional: 我同你坦白講，呢份報告做得唔夠好。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 nei5 taan2 baak6 gong2 ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 zou6 dak1 m4 gau3 hou2

rows.note: Use this colloquial phrase when stressing that someone speaks without sugar-coating.

example.english: He's always frank and says straight away if something is wrong.
example.traditional: 佢一向直腸直肚，有咩唔妥都會即刻講。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 hoeng3 zik6 coeng4 zik6 tou5 jau5 me1 m4 to5 dou1 wui5 zik1 hak1 gong2

rows.note: Use this when frankness is presented more generally as being honest or straightforward.

example.english: To be frank, I don't think this plan will work.
example.traditional: 老實講，我覺得呢個計劃唔會成功。
example.jyutping: lou5 sat6 gong2 ngo5 gok3 dak1 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 m4 wui5 sing4 gung1

rows.note: Use this more formal choice for sincere openness, especially when bluntness is not the focus.

example.english: During the meeting, both sides exchanged views in a frank manner.
example.traditional: 會議中，雙方以坦誠態度交換意見。
example.jyutping: wui6 ji5 zung1 soeng1 fong1 ji5 taan2 sing4 taai3 dou6 gaau1 wun6 ji3 gin3
